title: Research Assistant – LLM-Guided Linux Kernel Policy Optimization

what_i_did: Researched and developed a novel framework for LLM-assisted code generation and optimization within Linux kernel space, targeting Page Cache policy customization. Investigated how high-level performance objectives could be translated into safe, executable kernel policies generated or refined by LLMs. Instrumented the kernel using the eBPF framework to collect fine-grained runtime signals and observability metrics, including memory pressure, cache hit/miss ratios, I/O wait, and workload characteristics. Integrated Linux observability tools such as vmstat, uptime, and related system metrics to construct evaluator feature sets that were passed to LLMs for policy reasoning and generation. Extended the OpenEvolve framework in conjunction with eBPF hooks to enable controlled execution of custom kernel policies while maintaining system safety. Designed and implemented a robust validation and rollback pipeline to ensure generated policies did not violate kernel correctness, stability, or performance constraints. Benchmarked and compared existing page cache and storage optimization techniques, including ScaleCache, against LLM-driven policies. Evaluated system behavior across diverse, realistic workloads such as YCSB, FileIO, FileSearch, DuckDB analytical queries, and Twitter production traces, analyzing latency, throughput, and cache efficiency under varying access patterns.

title: Machine Learning Intern – Cipher Algorithm Detection
summary: Worked as a summer intern to design and productionize a machine-learning system for automatically detecting encryption and cipher algorithms from raw file content, aimed at improving security classification and data handling within Commvault’s storage pipeline.
what_i_did: Designed and implemented an end-to-end cipher detection pipeline, starting with extensive feature engineering on raw ciphertext inspired by NIST-style statistical tests. Engineered features such as Shannon entropy, block-level entropy variance, byte frequency distributions, n-gram repetition ratios, continuous run lengths, autocorrelation scores, chi-square randomness tests, byte transition matrices, and sliding-window entropy profiles. Ran 40+ controlled experiments to evaluate model families and inductive biases, including XGBoost, LightGBM, fully connected deep neural networks, CNNs over byte sequences, Transformer-based architectures, and BERT-style token models adapted for binary data. Experimented with multiple tokenization strategies to capture structural patterns across contiguous ciphertext blocks. Performed dimensionality reduction and exploratory analysis using t-SNE and UMAP to understand feature separability and failure modes. Selected and tuned a final model achieving ~80–85% accuracy with 0.70–0.75 F1 score. Productionized the solution by implementing a high-performance C++ feature extractor that reads the first ~40KB of file content, exports features to an ONNX-based inference pipeline, and integrates with Commvault’s product. Built and benchmarked parallel extractors, comparing streaming-based online extraction versus offline buffer-based approaches, achieving ~270ms extraction time per file.
